glance.title: Malaysia at a glance
source.label: Source
howto.line: Each line follows one group over the years. Click or tap a point to see its value.
caveat.dates: Figures are counted as at 1 January in earlier years and 30 June in recent years, so some points are 1.5 years apart.
caveat.over100: Completion rates can go above 100% because very few students drop out, and a small number repeat a grade or move between states.
def.students: Number of students enrolled in government schools.
def.teachers: Number of teachers in government primary and secondary schools.
def.schools: Number of government primary schools and government secondary schools.
def.completion: Share of students who complete a stage of education, relative to the cohort that started that stage.

caveat.axis90: The numbers on the left of the chart start at 90%, not 0%, so small changes can be seen.
q.leftout.unmatched: {n} district names are not shown because the two datasets spell, name or divide them differently.
q.leftout.small: {n} districts with very small numbers are not shown, because a ratio from small numbers can swing widely.
q.leftout.blank: {n} districts are not shown because no rate is published for them.
q.leftout.broken: {names}: not shown, because the figures jump sharply between two dates.
q.ratio.title: Which districts have the most and fewest students per teacher?
q.ratio.answer: As at {date}, among {n} districts, {a} has the most students per teacher ({av}) and {b} has the fewest ({bv}). Across Malaysia it is {m}.
q.ratio.counted: Students (primary and secondary) divided by teachers (primary and secondary) in government schools. This is our own calculation from two published counts, not an official ratio.
q.ratio.howto: Each row is one district. A higher number means more students for each teacher. It does not show the size of a class.
q.ratio.keep: The data does not say how teachers are counted (for example, whether a part-time teacher counts as one).
q.size.title: How many students does a primary school have, district by district?
q.size.answer: As at {date}, among {n} districts, a government primary school in {a} has {av} students on average, the most. In {b} it is {bv}, the fewest. Across Malaysia it is {m}.
q.size.counted: Primary students divided by the number of government primary schools. This is our own calculation from two published counts.
q.size.howto: Each row is one district. A lower number means smaller schools, on average.
q.size.keep: An average hides the largest and smallest schools in a district.
q.trend.title: Where is the number of primary students falling or rising?
q.trend.answer: Between {d1} and {d2}, the number of primary students fell most in {a} ({av}) and rose most in {b} ({bv}). Across Malaysia it changed by {m}.
q.trend.answer.range: Between {d1} and {d2}, the change in the number of primary students ranged from {av} in {a} to {bv} in {b}. Across Malaysia it changed by {m}.
q.trend.counted: Students enrolled in government primary schools on two dates, shown as a percentage change.
q.trend.howto: Each row is one state. A minus sign means fewer students than at the start; a plus sign means more.
q.trend.keep.districts: States only. Figures for many districts change sharply between 2022 and 2023, so districts are not compared over the years.
q.trend.keep.start: The comparison starts in 2018, because the 2017 figure for Perlis does not follow on from the later years.
q.completion.title: Where is upper secondary completion lowest?
q.completion.answer: As at {date}, among {n} districts, the upper secondary completion rate is lowest in {a} ({av}). Among states it is lowest in {s} ({sv}). Across Malaysia it is {m}.
q.completion.howto: Each row is one place. A lower rate means fewer students finished upper secondary, compared with the group that started it.
q.completion.keep.small: Small districts can swing a lot from year to year.
q.completion.keep.offices: District figures follow the areas of the District Education Offices, so they can differ from the state figures.
home.questions.title: Questions the data can answer
home.questions.lead: Each question links to the full ranked list, district by district or state by state.
